FALSE POSITIVE ON THE GATE'S OWN REMEDY. `initial={{ ...ENTER_INITIAL, opacity: 0 }}` — using the shared enter variants, which is literally what the deny message instructs — is BLOCKED, because the spread hides scale and blur from the substring test. 4. fix.name: no-select-star-sensitive.py
fix.defect: Two reproduced defect families, both false negatives on the exact leak the gate exists to stop. (1) SPELLING. SELECT_STAR = \.select\(\s*(['"`])\*\1 requires the closing quote immediately after the star, so .select("*, <anything>") never matches. That is the canonical Supabase idiom for "all base columns plus an embedded resource", and it is the spelling THIS codebase uses: the repo's own backend audit (recovered from project session transcripts) names app/api/salons/route.ts:88 as .select(`*, services(...)`) under the finding "Salon search + PDP ship all 101 salon columns (select *) to anonymous clients", plus app/api/availability/[salon_id]/route.ts:20 and app/api/profile/favorites. All three are in the gate's scope, on tables in its SENSITIVE set, and all three pass. app/api/bookings/route.ts:140 blocks only incidentally via its nested salons(*), not via its own base-table star. (2) TOOL SHAPE. The gate classifies sensitivity by scanning backward from the star for .from("<table>"). On an Edit it receives only the replacement fragment, which almost never contains the .from(, so a minimal surgical edit that re-introduces select("*") is invisible. The project's own "surgical edits only, never rewrite a whole file" rule means the one shape the gate reliably catches (a Write carrying both calls in one string) is the shape its house rules discourage. Its 12-case self-test drives Write exclusively, which is why this was never exercised. Also reproduced: salons!inner(*) and reviews!review_salon_fk(*) pass while salon:salons(*) blocks (NESTED_JOIN_STAR captures "inner"/"review_salon_fk" as the table name); bare .select() passes though supabase-js defaults that argument to '*'; a MultiEdit payload passes although MultiEdit is in the registered settings matcher, because nothing
